transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Well, I guess what made me come in is that I just keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody. It's... I don't know, I just feel like I'm a fake in my apprenticeship. Like I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices, over stuff that I know other people would probably just fix the mistake and move on from. But I just can't seem to shake it, and it's really getting to me.
Along with feeling like you've ruined things, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or empty?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty, really. It's just more... this heavy feeling that I'm messing everything up, like I said. But not sad.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy doing?

Yeah, I guess I have. Um... lately, I can just walk right past my sketchbook, or skip volleyball, and I just completely ignore the group texts for my volunteer stuff. I do it without really feeling much of anything. It's weird because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? But now I just don't really care to do them.
How long have you been feeling this way and experiencing this loss of interest?
I'd say... it's been about nine months now. It's just been this long stretch. I think it really became a lot harder to hide once my classes and my apprenticeship work started slipping.
How has your sleep been during these past nine months?

It's been pretty all over the place. Um, for a while, I was actually getting by on just three or four hours a night, and I'd still show up completely wired for the job and my classes. But now... now I either just can't fall asleep at all, or I wake up way before my alarm and feel like I never even rested.
During that time when you were sleeping so little and felt wired, did you feel like you had much more energy than usual?

Yeah, I really did. It felt like... I just had this nonstop charge in my body. Like, after a full day working on the pipes, I would still go to my evening classes, and then I'd come home and just keep going. I'd reorganize all my tools, clean my whole apartment, and then start drawing out plumbing systems instead of just sitting down for a minute. I just never really felt the need to stop.
How long did that period of having nonstop energy and needing so little sleep last?
Um... I'd say that whole pattern went on for about five months. It started right after I began a sustainable plumbing certification, which was on top of my regular apprenticeship.
